name: Election and Predestination

objectives.text: Identify from Ephesians 1:4 that the Bible says God chose His people in Christ before the world began
Recall that the Bible describes God's choosing of His people as a gift of His love and not something they earned
Recall Jesus' words that His disciples did not choose Him but He chose them
Describe how Jeremiah 1:5 and Psalm 139:16 show that God knew and planned for people before they were born
Summarize election as God's free and gracious choice of a people in Christ to be saved
Explain what Ephesians 1:5 means when it says God predestined His people for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ
Define the terms decree, foreknowledge, predestination, and election using Scripture and the Westminster Standards
Compare election by grace with being chosen on the basis of works using Paul's argument in Romans 11 and 2 Timothy 1
Explain how the Reformed tradition presents election as a ground for the believer's assurance and humility
Explain why the tradition teaches that God ordains the means of salvation as well as its end so that election does not make preaching, prayer, or faith unnecessary
Analyze Romans 9:11-16 to show why the Reformed tradition holds that election is unconditional and not grounded in foreseen faith or works
Distinguish the biblical sense of foreknowledge as God's prior set love from mere foresight of future choices
Interpret Romans 9:13 in light of its Old Testament sources in Genesis 25 and Malachi 1
Explain how election connects to the eternal covenant of redemption in which the Father gives a people to the Son
Explain the doctrine of reprobation as the tradition confesses it, distinguishing God's passing by of some from their condemnation for their own sin
Explain how the tradition holds together election with the free offer of the gospel to all and human responsibility to believe
Explain why the Westminster Confession and the Canons of Dort counsel that predestination be taught with special care and reverence
Construct a diagram of the golden chain in Romans 8:29-30 that explains each link from foreknowledge to glorification
Summarize the Remonstrant controversy and the Synod of Dort's response on the doctrine of election
Evaluate the Arminian view of conditional election against the Reformed view using the relevant biblical texts
Defend the justice and freedom of God in election by responding to the objections Paul answers in Romans 9
Compare the infralapsarian and supralapsarian views of the order of God's decrees and identify which view the Canons of Dort reflect
Compose a theological essay that synthesizes how Scripture and the confessions present election as a ground for humility, assurance, and gospel mission

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies, including the definition of election, adoption as goal, grace versus works, unconditional election, Romans 9:13, covenant of redemption, reprobation, golden chain, the Arminian comparison, God's justice, and the closing synthesis. Recast the grade 6 'apply the comfort' objective as explaining the tradition's teaching on election and assurance, so it no longer targets a feeling. Replaced the vague grade 2 and 3 items with specific text-based ones (John 15:16, Jeremiah 1:5, Psalm 139:16). Added missing competencies: key-term definitions, means and ends, foreknowledge as set love, election and the free offer, the confessions' pastoral counsel on teaching predestination, the Synod of Dort history, and infra/supralapsarianism. Anchored each objective to specific verses and confessional articles, using Westminster, Canons of Dort, and Heidelberg citations in the required format.
